json.reason: Recurring, syntactically detectable API misuse: converting a plain decimal currency amount to integer cents with floating-point arithmetic (Math.round(x * 100)) instead of the project's toCents() helper.
json.title: Currency amount converted to cents with floating-point math instead of toCents()
json.message: Math.round($AMOUNT * 100) is off by one cent for some values (0.29 * 100 === 28.999999999999996); use toCents($AMOUNT)
json.note: Multiplying a decimal currency amount by 100 in binary floating point can land just below the .5 boundary, so Math.round rounds down and the result is one cent too low. Use the shared toCents() helper from ./money for exact decimal-to-cents conversion. This only applies to a plain amount value; rounding the result of a computed rate (e.g. amount * FEE_RATE * 100) is intentional business rounding and is not flagged.
json.rule_yaml:
rule:
  any:
    - pattern: Math.round($AMOUNT * 100)
    - pattern: Math.round(100 * $AMOUNT)
constraints:
  AMOUNT:
    any:
      - kind: identifier
      - kind: member_expression
      - kind: number
